risk_if_not_implemented: Without Information Leakage Due To Electromagnetic Signals Emanations, unauthorized individuals may gain physical access to facilities and equipment, enabling theft, tampering, damage or safety incidents. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to natural threats NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-8, NT-11, NT-12, NT-13, NT-14; Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Product Defect / Design Failure (MT-23).

compensating_control_1.name: Physical Security of Offices, Rooms & Facilities
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to identify systems, equipment and respective operating environments that require limited physical access so that appropriate physical access controls are designed and implemented for offices, rooms and facilities.
compensating_control_1.justification: Physical Security of Offices, Rooms & Facilities (PES-10) provides physical access control that compensates for the absence of Information Leakage Due To Electromagnetic Signals Emanations (PES-30) by preventing unauthorized physical interaction with systems and infrastructure. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation)
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to implement network segmentation within network architectures to isolate Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS) from other network resources.
compensating_control_2.justification: Network Segmentation (macrosegmentation) (NET-06) provides network-level access restriction that compensates for the absence of Information Leakage Due To Electromagnetic Signals Emanations (PES-30) by limiting attacker reach and lateral movement opportunities across the environment. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
